The '''M-towers''', also known as the '''Metropolis Towers''', are three towers that are proposed between triq d'Argens and triq Testaferrata within the limits of [[Msida]], [[Malta]], though often mentioned at [[Gżira]] and commonly known as the "Testaferrata site". The tallest of the three towers, at 33 stories, would become the [[List of tallest buildings in Malta|second tallest building on the island]], only behind the [[Mercury Tower]]. The towers would form part of a larger project, ''Metropolis Plaza'', to include a plaza, shops and restaurants.<ref>{{cite news|last1=Macdonald|first1=Vanessa|title=Aiming high|url=http://www.timesofmalta.com/articles/view/20070705/business/aiming-high.179883|accessdate=22 February 2015|work=[[Times of Malta]]|date=5 July 2007}}</ref><ref>{{cite news|title=Reaching new heights|url=http://www.timesofmalta.com/articles/view/20071209/business/reaching-new-heights.187611|accessdate=22 February 2015|work=[[Times of Malta]]|date=9 December 2007}}</ref> 
The building is set to affect the skyline of Valletta and the Grand Harbour. The Gzira Local Council did not object to the project.<ref name=azzopardi/>
Until early 2023, the project was on hold and no development had taken place on site for years.<ref>[http://global.ctbuh.org/resources/papers/download/1207-urban-design-strategy-report-on-tall-buildings-in-malta.pdf p. 7]</ref> However, works on the site resumed in February 2023.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Lasys |first=Arnas |date=2023-02-13 |title=Works on Gzira's Metropolis high-rise finally continuing after years-long pause |url=https://businessnow.mt/works-on-gziras-metropolis-high-rise-finally-continuing-after-years-long-pause/ |access-date=2023-05-11 |website=BusinessNow.mt |language=en-US}}</ref>

== Site ==
The Metropolis project is being built on the site of the former Mira building, which since 1939 hosted the Mamo Brothers garage. The building was one of the few [[Art Nouveau]]/[[Art Deco]] buildings in Malta.

In the late 1970s, ''Mamo Brothers (1939) Ltd'' and its Mira building was taken over by the Zammit group formed by the sons of Eucharist Zammit who in the 1960s used to run the [[Gozo ferry|Malta-Gozo ferries]].<ref>[https://www.zamgroup.com/about Zammit Group]</ref> The new Mira Motor Sales Ltd company was the Malta importer of [[Vauxhall Motors|Vauxhall]] automobiles, and introduced [[BMW]] to Malta, though the later lost the brand to [[Muscats Motors]]. They also sold [[Isuzu]] and [[Honda]].

== Planning and development ==
A consortium of Maltese entrepreneurs (including today's GlobalCapital) bought the site in 2006 and launched the real estate project on the Testaferrata site, foreseeing “a lifestyle building with all apartments having their own view and large terraces”.<ref name=dalli2015>[https://www.maltatoday.com.mt/news/national/51547/120_million_metropolis_project_to_be_completed_in_three_years_time#.XqwTb_gzY2w Malta Today], 2015</ref>

The project was aimed at giving new life to Testaferrata Street, which was associated with [[prostitution]].<ref>{{cite news|last1=Fenech|first1=Gerald|title=Gzira to switch off the red light|url=http://archive.maltatoday.com.mt/2007/08/05/n10.html|accessdate=22 February 2015|work=[[Malta Today]]|date=5 August 2007}}</ref>

Construction of the towers was supposed to start in 2007 and was estimated to be complete by 2016. The project was estimated to cost €60 million. However, the project was delayed by a number of years due to a lack of finance and permits.<ref name=azzopardi>[https://andrewazzopardi.wordpress.com/2013/11/18/prostitutes-to-relocate-due-to-tallest-building-project-maltatoday/ Andrew Azzopardi], Malta Today, 2013</ref>

The land was then sold to developer Jalal Husni Bey, from [[Libya]]'s [[HB Group]],<ref>[https://timesofmalta.com/articles/view/The-defiant-developer.507552 The Defiant Developer], ''Times of Malta'', 2014</ref> who had originally foreseen "buy[ing] some apartments.<ref name=dalli2015/><ref>[http://www.metropolis.com.mt/promoters.html Metropolis.com.mt], Promoters</ref>

The project was initially approved by the [[Malta Environment and Planning Authority]] (MEPA) on 12 March 2009.<ref>{{cite news|title=MEPA approves Gzira high-rise development|url=http://www.timesofmalta.com/articles/view/20090312/local/mepa-approves-gzira-high-rise-development.248516|accessdate=22 February 2015|work=[[Times of Malta]]|date=12 March 2009}}</ref>

In 2013, Gzira mayor Roberto Cristiano claimed the building would give the locality "a fresh look" and "increase the value of surrounding properties" as well as "increase economic activity in Gzira and may also attract other investment opportunities". He conceded that it would also increase traffic and parking problems.<ref name=azzopardi/>

In November 2014, MEPA approved a number of changes to the Metropolis project, including building a [[helipad]] on the roof of the highest tower, a larger car park and the creation of more public places.<ref>{{cite news|title=Gzira's Metropolis Towers project to get more parking spaces, helipad|url=http://www.timesofmalta.com/articles/view/20141110/local/gziras-metropolis-towers-project-to-get-more-parking-spaces-helipad.543433|accessdate=22 February 2015|work=[[Times of Malta]]|date=10 November 2014}}</ref> The project was then estimated at €100 million, almost double the original estimate.

The first stone was laid by Prime Minister [[Joseph Muscat]] on 6 April 2015, few days ahead the [[2015 Maltese local elections]],<ref>{{cite news|title=Foundation stone of the Metropolis Plaza in Gzira laid|url=http://www.timesofmalta.com/articles/view/20150406/local/foundation-stone-of-the-metropolis-plaza-in-gzira-laid.562885|accessdate=6 April 2015|work=[[Times of Malta]]|date=6 April 2015}}</ref> 
The early phase of construction was to be delivered by Maltese contractor [[Polidano Group|Polidano]], while the towers would be constructed by an Italian and a Dubai-based company, whose names were not disclosed.<ref name=dalli2015/>
Nevertheless, no actual works followed, and the foundation stone was later removed. 
By 2017, it was claimed that the project had still not secured financing.<ref>[https://timesofmalta.com/articles/view/whatever-happened-to-the-metropolis-mega-development.644590 Times of Malta], 2017</ref> 
The excavated site remains known by the locals as "the big hole".

According to the representative of the developer, the delays were due to the need to create more parking spaces around the towers. Since the land surrounding the project was not government-owned, the government requisitioned it, and the Lands Authority in October 2016 issued a tender to ensure that Metropolis could obtain access to the space beneath the roads and excavate for two further floors underground, beneath sea level.<ref>[https://www.maltatoday.com.mt/environment/townscapes/85743/stalled_metropolis_highrise_in_gzira_considering_further_excavation Malta Today], 2018</ref>

Husni Bey claimed that “high rise projects usually scare a lot of people because they would not be used to it. However, we have to recognise that they are a must and every country should have a designated area for high rise buildings.”<ref name=dalli2015/> Husni Bey praised Malta's prime minister [[Joseph Muscat]] and those “calling the shots who have been very helpful”, while describing as "very painful" the process of dealing with the [[Malta Environment and Planning Authority]].<ref name=dalli2015/>

In 2019, Husni Bey's business partner Keith Seychell claimed that the project is still on the table, but that Husni Bey could not find a general contractor to take it forward.<ref>[https://www.businesstoday.com.mt/people/people/95/interview__keith_seychell_the_joy_of_closing_a_deal_food_quality_and_karma#.XqwTgPgzY2w Business Today]</ref>

A social impact assessment study carried out in August 2019 found great construction fatigue among residents of  Gzira, Msida and Ta’ Xbiex. Nearly two thirds of them disagreed with the Metropolis projects and other towers proposed for the same area. Residents lamented in particular 
air, noise and [[visual pollution]], growing difficulties in finding parking, and growing distrust towards the construction industry.
41% insisted there were no positive impacts to the locality.<ref>[https://www.maltatoday.com.mt/environment/townscapes/100925/mistrust_and_resentment_over_testaferrata_street_highrise_62_say_no_to_new_tower Malta Today], March 2020</ref>
